title: GC-move-across-unrooted-Term — the JIT runtime helpers that write pre-move Term pointers and read pre-move slices after a collecting allocation (H3, H4; H5 owned elsewhere)

purpose:
Ground: `docs/REVIEW-23-07.md` (reviewed at `fd71c5e`, 2026-07-23), recommended priority order item 2 — "H3, H4, H5 — the GC-move-across-unrooted-Term class in JIT runtime helpers and string BIFs; audit the whole crate for `Term`/slice held across `ensure_space`/`alloc_*`". Re-pinned at build base `a0359a2` by reading the bytes; every location below is CURRENT, not the review's.

THE CLASS. beamr's collector is a per-process generational COPYING collector. `gc::ensure_space` (`crates/beamr/src/gc/mod.rs:149-170`) runs `collect_minor_with_live` and, on its failure, `collect_major`; a minor collection physically relocates live young-heap objects and then `HeapRegion::reset()` zero-fills the vacated young region. Roots are the X/Y register file (bounded by `live_x`) plus `Process::native_roots` (`crates/beamr/src/process/mod.rs:584` enumerates them into the root set, `:646` forwards them after the walk). A `Term` value held in a Rust local, or a `&[u8]` laundered out of a `BinaryRef`, is NOT a root and is NOT forwarded. Any such capture that is USED after a call which can reach `ensure_space` reads relocated-or-zeroed memory. Because the vacated region is zero-filled rather than poisoned, the face of the defect is SILENT CORRUPTION — no error, no crash, no log.

THE EXISTING DISCIPLINE (the pattern this brief restores, cited concretely). The interpreter already gets this right, at the exact twins of the two defective JIT helpers:
- `crates/beamr/src/interpreter/opcodes/binary/matching.rs:24-72` `bs_start_match` — the interpreter twin of `jit_bs_start_match`. Its comment at `:41-42` is the doctrine verbatim: "Reserve before reading the source: GC moves heap terms, and registers are the only roots, so no term may be held across a collection." It calls `gc::ensure_space(process, MATCH_CONTEXT_WORDS, 256)` at `:43`, THEN reads the source operand at `:44`, then allocates with the BARE non-collecting `heap_mut().alloc()` at `:61-64`, and only then writes `heap[3] = source.raw()` at `:69`.
- `crates/beamr/src/interpreter/opcodes/binary/matching.rs:207-235` `bs_get_tail` — the interpreter twin of `jit_bs_get_binary`. Comment at `:225-226`: "The tail size depends on the context, so reserve after sizing and then re-read the (possibly moved) context before touching its bytes." Reserve at `:228`, RE-READ the context at `:229`, slice at `:230`, allocate at `:231`.
- `crates/beamr/src/interpreter/opcodes/closures.rs:443-488` `put_map` — the interpreter twin of `jit_map_update`. Comment at `:462-467`: the `ensure_space` "must run BEFORE any term is copied into the Rust vectors below, and a safety-net collection moves the source map, so the map is re-read from its operand afterwards." `ensure_space` at `:476`, re-read at `:477-480`, and only then the update vector is built at `:482-488`.
This is the "heap-allocating lowerings re-read operands after alloc" discipline the review lists among the JIT's strengths (REVIEW-23-07.md:133). The three defects below are the sites where it was not applied.

THE DEFECTS, RE-PINNED AT `a0359a2`.

(H3) `crates/beamr/src/jit/runtime_binary_match.rs:36` — UNCHANGED from the review's pin. `jit_bs_start_match` binds `let source = Term::from_raw(binary)` at `:21`, calls `alloc_words(process, MATCH_CONTEXT_WORDS)` at `:28`, and writes `heap[3] = source.raw()` at `:36`. `alloc_words` (`crates/beamr/src/jit/runtime.rs:338-351`) calls `gc::ensure_space(process, words, 256)` at `:343` — a full collecting entry. `live_x = 256` forwards the X registers, so the caller's copy of the binary survives and moves; the helper's by-value `source` local does not. The match context is therefore built pointing at the pre-move address. Every subsequent `jit_bs_get_integer` / `jit_bs_get_binary` / `jit_bs_get_utf*` on that context reads through `JitMatchContext::source_term()` (`:152-154`) → `source()` (`:155-157`) → `as_bytes()` (`:175`) at the dead address.

(H3-b, NEW AT RE-PIN — see R5) `crates/beamr/src/jit/runtime_binary_match.rs:175` — `JitMatchContext::slice()` returns `self.source()?.as_bytes().get(start..end)`, an `&'static [u8]` over process-heap words when the source is an inline `Binary` (≤ 64 B, `REFC_BINARY_THRESHOLD`) or a `SubBinary` over one. `jit_bs_get_binary` takes that slice at `:91-93` and passes it to `allocate_extracted_binary` at `:94`; for a non-ProcBin source that reaches `allocate_binary` (`:243-256`), whose FIRST act is `alloc_words` at `:245` → `ensure_space` → collect, and which only then copies the borrow at `:255` `alloc_binary(heap, bytes)`. This is a textbook crossing of the AUDIT.md class, and AUDIT.md classifies `jit/runtime_binary_match.rs:175` as SAFE (line 98, under "Read-only consumption, no allocation while live"). That verdict is correct for `jit_bs_get_integer` and the three `get_utf*` decoders, which consume the slice into an integer before any allocation; it is WRONG for `jit_bs_get_binary`, whose consumer allocates. The audit's SAFE row is per-SITE, but the site has multiple consumers with different fates. The sibling verdict at `jit/runtime_binary_build.rs:90` was re-checked at the bytes and is CORRECT SAFE: `jit_bs_put_binary` writes the borrow into a pre-existing builder buffer at `:97` with no allocation in between.

(H4) `crates/beamr/src/jit/runtime_map.rs:135` — UNCHANGED from the review's pin. `write_map_entries` builds the `keys` and `values` `Vec<Term>` at `:130-134`, calls `gc::ensure_space(process, words, 256)` at `:135`, allocates at `:138`, and writes the PRE-MOVE terms at `:139` `write_map(heap, &keys, &values)`. The entries come from `map_entries(source_map)` (`:120-126`, reading `Term`s straight out of the source map's heap words) and from `map_pair_terms` (`:91-110`, reading raw term words out of a JIT stack slot via `from_raw_parts`); neither the Rust `Vec`s nor the generated-code stack slot are GC roots. `live_x = 256` forwards the X registers, so the surviving copies move and the vectors are left holding dead addresses. The resulting map's keys and values point into the zero-filled young region. This is not a corner: any `#{...}` update in JIT-compiled code whose keys or values are boxed (binaries, bigints, tuples, nested maps, cons cells) and whose map words do not fit the nursery remainder hits it.

(H5) `crates/beamr/src/native/stdlib_stubs/string_bifs.rs` — SCOPED OUT, OWNED ELSEWHERE. Re-pinned and unchanged at `a0359a2`: the launder is `binary_bytes` at `:339-343` (`BinaryRef::new(term).map(|binary| binary.as_bytes())` → `Result<&'static [u8], Term>`) with `utf8_str` at `:335-337` on top of it; the consumers are `bif_trim` `:64`, `bif_split` `:86`, `bif_find` `:98`, `bif_pad` `:152`, `bif_slice` `:208`. Cross-referenced against `docs/design/beamr/briefs/evidence/aion-encode-gc-defect/asbytes-sweep/AUDIT.md` (lane 3, Artemis Peach's scope of record, sweep base `f684d60`): these are audit sites 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 of the eleven REAL crossings. ALL FOUR consumers the review names (split/find/trim/slice) are owned; the audit additionally owns `bif_pad`, which the review missed. H5 is therefore ENTIRELY inside the pending 0.16.3 backport's mechanical-ten lane and this brief does not touch that file. The residue the backport's own fix shape leaves behind — `binary_bytes`/`utf8_str` continue to hand out `&'static` borrows of GC-managed memory, so the next author to add a `string:*` BIF re-arms the same trap — is recorded in R6's table as a follow-on, not fixed here (touching the file would collide with the backport at exactly the lines it edits).

AION EXPOSURE (why the sequencing matters). AUDIT.md's reachability section establishes that all eleven owned sites are registered by the registration sets aion's embedding loads and are live in DEPLOYED 0.16.2. The three sites in THIS brief are JIT-runtime helpers: they execute only for JIT-compiled bodies, so their exposure surface is narrower and their severity picture is separate from the backport's. That difference is the reason the two lanes can be sequenced independently and the reason this brief must not be folded into the backport.

WHY THE FIX IS NOT THE INTERPRETER'S. The interpreter's shape — reserve, then RE-READ the operand — is unavailable verbatim inside a JIT helper: generated code passes the term BY VALUE across the C ABI (`crates/beamr/src/jit/compiler/ir_helpers.rs:334-340` declares `beamr_jit_bs_start_match` as `(I64, I64) -> I64`; `:305-311` declares `beamr_jit_map_update` as four `I64`s), so the helper has no operand to re-read from. The tree already ships the facility that closes the gap: `Process::push_native_root` / `native_root` / `truncate_native_roots` (`crates/beamr/src/process/mod.rs:871-908`, `pub(crate)`, so the `jit` module can call them), whose slots ARE enumerated as roots at `:584` and forwarded at `:646`. This is the same machinery `ProcessContext::with_rooted` (`crates/beamr/src/native/context/mod.rs:807-832`) exposes to native BIFs, and which `bif_next_grapheme` (`string_bifs.rs:123-135`) already uses correctly.
task:
DESIGN STANCE (decided; one carved fork, OQ-A). Three sites, one class, one repair shape: NO capture may outlive a call that can reach `gc::ensure_space`. Each site is repaired by making the capture a root across the collection and re-reading it afterwards, or by moving the reserve ahead of the capture so no collection can occur in the span. Zero behavioural change on the non-collecting path; zero new configuration; zero new wake paths.

D1 — ROOT-ACROSS-ALLOC IN THE JIT HELPERS (recommended shape; the fork is OQ-A). Add a small private helper in `crates/beamr/src/jit/runtime.rs` alongside `alloc_words` — working name `alloc_words_rooting(process, words, roots: &mut [Term]) -> *mut u64` — that pushes each `Term` in `roots` via `Process::push_native_root`, calls the existing `alloc_words`, reads the forwarded values back via `Process::native_root`, writes them into the caller's slice, truncates to the entry depth, and returns the pointer. It must truncate on the null/failure return path too. Doc comment carries the doctrine sentence from `matching.rs:41-42` and names the `native_roots` root-set and forwarding sites (`process/mod.rs:584`, `:646`) so the next reader can verify the claim without tracing.

D2 — H3 MINT. `jit_bs_start_match` (`runtime_binary_match.rs:17-38`) routes its `MATCH_CONTEXT_WORDS` allocation through D1 with `source` in the root slice, and writes the POST-collection `source` into `heap[3]`. `total_bits` is computed from the length, which a move does not change, so it may be computed either side; the brief's preference is to keep the existing order and re-read only the term, minimising the diff. The `BinaryRef::new` refusal and both early returns (`0` for a null process/failed alloc, `BINARY_HELPER_FAILURE` for a non-binary or overflow) keep their exact current values — generated code branches on them.

D3 — H3-b MINT. `jit_bs_get_binary` (`runtime_binary_match.rs:66-99`) adopts the `bs_get_tail` shape: size the extraction, RESERVE, re-derive the slice from the (possibly moved) match context, then allocate. Concretely: hoist the reserve out of `allocate_extracted_binary`/`allocate_binary` for this caller by calling `gc::ensure_space` for the computed word count with the match-context term rooted via D1, then take `context.slice(bits)` AFTER the reserve, then let `allocate_binary`'s own `alloc_words` run as a no-op because the space is already available — exactly as `bs_get_tail` does at `matching.rs:228-231`. The match-context term itself must be rooted, not merely the source: the context is a heap-allocated boxed object and moves too, and `JitMatchContext` holds a bare `*mut u64`. NOTE the ProcBin arm of `allocate_extracted_binary` (`:265-273`) also allocates (`alloc_words(process, SUB_BINARY_WORDS)` at `:268`) and then writes `source` — the same stale-Term shape as H3, on a term captured at `:264`. It is IMMUNE to the byte-corruption face (ProcBin bytes are off-heap and Arc-retained) but NOT to the stale-pointer face: the `source` written into the sub-binary at `:273` is a pre-move ProcBin box address. Repair it under the same D1 call; it is in scope.

D4 — H4 MINT. `write_map_entries` (`runtime_map.rs:128-140`) adopts the `put_map` shape: the reserve moves BEFORE the terms are copied into Rust vectors. Because `write_map_entries` receives `entries` already built by `map_update` (`:52-89`), the honest repair is at `map_update`'s level — reserve the upper-bound word count (`map_word_count(source_map.len() + pair_count)`) BEFORE `map_entries`/`map_pair_terms` run, then build the vectors, sort, and write with a bare non-collecting allocation. That mirrors `put_map`'s `words_bound` computation at `closures.rs:468-476` including its deliberate refusal to trust a `live` operand. The `exact` (`is_map_update` vs `map_new`) refusal at `:68-76` and every `return 0` failure value are preserved byte-for-byte. If the drafter finds the bound arithmetic materially harder to keep overflow-safe at `map_update`'s level than to root the vectors at `write_map_entries`' level, D1-rooting of the two vectors is an acceptable alternative — state the choice and its reasoning in the handoff; the acceptance criteria are written to the observable behaviour, not to the shape.

D5 — THE AUDIT CORRECTION IS A DELIVERABLE, NOT A FOOTNOTE. `AUDIT.md` is the standing record of the as_bytes borrow-across-alloc class and the authority the 0.16.3 backport's scope is drawn from. A site moving SAFE → REAL changes that authority. R5 amends the record in place, forward-only (the house evidence convention: correct by appending a dated correction block, never by rewriting a landed verdict), and the amendment is escalated to the domain owner BEFORE the fix commits land, so the backport lane's builder can decide whether he wants the site. The default answer is that he does not — it is JIT code, outside every lane of the backport, and RF-006 is already repairing it — but that is the domain owner's call, not the drafter's.

D6 — THE PRIORITY-2 RIDER IS ITS OWN REQUIREMENT WITH ITS OWN ARTIFACT. The review's rider is "audit the whole crate for `Term`/slice held across `ensure_space`/`alloc_*`". Its relationship to AUDIT.md must be stated honestly in the artifact itself, because the two are COMPLEMENTARY and NEITHER SUBSUMES THE OTHER: AUDIT.md swept SLICE borrows, enumerated by grepping the `as_bytes` accessor family (`BinaryRef`/`Binary`/`ProcBin`/`SubBinary`) and tracing receiver types — 68 sites, 11 real. This rider sweeps stale TERM and RAW-POINTER captures — a `Term` local, a `Vec<Term>`, a `*mut u64`/`*const u64` into heap words, or a struct wrapping one (`JitMatchContext` is the worked example) — held across a call that can reach `ensure_space`. H3, H3-b's ProcBin arm and H4 are all in the rider's shape and NONE of them appear in AUDIT.md's 68. H3-b is in BOTH shapes, which is why the audit found the site and mis-verdicted the consumer. The deliverable is a site table in AUDIT.md's own format (site / function / capture span → crossing / verdict / immunity reason), every verdict verified at the bytes at the builder's seat, with the total enumerated and the real-crossing count stated.

OQ-A — CARVED, FOR THE TEAR. D1 (in-helper native rooting) versus ALT-1 (move the reserve into the LOWERING: emit a `beamr_jit_test_heap` call — the helper exists at `crates/beamr/src/jit/runtime.rs:247-261` and already wraps `gc::ensure_space` — before the operand is materialised into the ABI argument register, so the helper allocates from pre-reserved space and can never collect). ALT-1 is arguably the more faithful analogue of the interpreter, since it puts the reserve where the operands are still in registers and therefore still roots. It is NOT recommended for v1: it requires a static word-count bound at compile time for a match context (fine, it is the constant `MATCH_CONTEXT_WORDS`) but ALSO for a map update (whose bound depends on the runtime source-map size, which the lowering does not know), so it would fix H3 and leave H4 needing D1 anyway — two mechanisms for one class. D1 is one mechanism, entirely inside the runtime helpers, uses a facility already in the tree and already GC-integrated, and leaves the generated code byte-identical (a real virtue: no new deopt edges, no change to the compiled-code surface the conformance job pins). Recorded for the tear to rule.

requirements.title: RED — three GC-motion walls that fail at the current bytes
requirements.spec:
Per the red-first bar: before any fix, three forced-geometry walls that are RED at build base `a0359a2` and go green only with R2/R3/R4. House pattern to mirror, cited: `crates/beamr/src/native/stdlib_stubs/json_bifs_tests.rs:222-249` (`multibyte_binary_moved_by_minor_gc_encodes_byte_exact` — allocate an inline binary, park it in X0, allocate filler cons cells, `collect_minor`, assert the register value MOVED via `assert_ne!`, then exercise the subject on the forwarded term) and `:251-299` (`encode_result_allocation_collects_with_multibyte_input_live` — the forced-geometry wall: compute `needed` via `alloc_binary_word_count`, fill the nursery with `alloc_cons` until `available() < needed`, ASSERT that precondition explicitly, assert `old_used() == 0` before, assert `old_used() > 0` after to prove a collection actually ran, and assert the live input was promoted via `assert_ne!` on the register). Both riders from that lane apply: the collection must be ASSERTED to have happened, not assumed, and the precondition must be asserted, not arranged and trusted. The JIT helpers are `pub(crate) extern "C"` and are directly callable from an in-crate `#[cfg(test)] mod` — precedent in the same file at `runtime_binary_match.rs:382-407` (`mod gc_release_tests`, which calls `allocate_binary` directly against a bare `Process::new`); `process_from_abi` (`runtime.rs:327-336`) only rejects null, so `&mut process as *mut Process` is a valid test argument and no scheduler is required.

W1 (H3): build an inline (≤ 64 B) binary, hold it in X0, fill the nursery so `MATCH_CONTEXT_WORDS` cannot fit, call `jit_bs_start_match`, then read the produced context's bytes back through a `jit_bs_get_binary`/`jit_bs_get_integer` extraction and assert byte-exactness against the original. Assert the collection ran and that X0 moved.

W2 (H3-b): build an inline binary, start a match context on it with space available, THEN fill the nursery so the extraction allocation must collect, call `jit_bs_get_binary`, and assert the extracted binary's bytes equal the expected source range. Assert collection ran and the source moved.

W3 (H4): build a source map whose keys and/or values are BOXED heap terms (inline binaries are the clearest — their corruption is visible as bytes), fill the nursery so the merged map's words cannot fit, call `jit_map_update` (or `map_update` directly), and assert every key and value in the result compares equal to its original. Assert collection ran.
acceptance: All three walls RED at `a0359a2` with the corruption face RECORDED — the observed wrong bytes/terms captured verbatim in the evidence run logs, not merely 'assertion failed'. Zero-filled reads are the expected face (`HeapRegion::reset()` zero-fills the vacated young region); if any wall reds with a segfault or garbage instead, that is a DIFFERENT failure and the drafter STOPs and reports before proceeding

Each wall asserts its own forced-geometry precondition (`available() < needed`) AND that a collection actually ran (`old_used()` transition), per the walls-lane-1 riders — a wall that passes because no collection occurred is a false green and is rejected

Each wall is red for the RIGHT reason: one minimal semantic mutation per wall, committed as a diff file with its observed red run under `docs/design/beamr/briefs/evidence/review-23-07/rf-006/mutations/` + `runs/`, never applied to the tree — the walls-lane-1 mutation-evidence convention
Walls live in `#[cfg(test)]` modules in the files under repair (house pattern per `gc_release_tests`); no new integration-test file is required and none is added

requirements.title: The rooting facility — alloc-across-roots in the JIT runtime
requirements.spec: Per D1: a private helper in `crates/beamr/src/jit/runtime.rs` that roots a caller-supplied set of `Term`s across `alloc_words`, using `Process::push_native_root` / `native_root` / `truncate_native_roots` (`process/mod.rs:871-908`), and hands the caller back the FORWARDED values. Truncates to entry depth on every exit path including the null/allocation-failure return. Doc comment names the root-set enumeration site (`process/mod.rs:584`) and the forwarding site (`:646`) and carries the doctrine sentence from `matching.rs:41-42`.
acceptance: Root depth is restored on every path — success, null process, `words == 0`, and `ensure_space` failure — proven by a unit test asserting `native_root_depth()` is unchanged across each
Returned terms are the POST-collection values: a unit test forces a collection inside the helper and asserts the handed-back `Term` differs from the one passed in and resolves to the same bytes
No new `#[allow]`, no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`, no `_ =>` arm

requirements.title: H3 + H3-b — the binary-match helpers stop writing pre-move pointers and stop reading pre-move slices
requirements.spec: Per D2 and D3: `jit_bs_start_match` writes the post-collection source into the match context; `jit_bs_get_binary` reserves, then re-derives the slice from the possibly-moved context, then allocates — the `bs_get_tail` shape at `matching.rs:225-231`; `allocate_extracted_binary`'s ProcBin arm writes the post-collection source term into the sub-binary. All refusal values and early-return codes are preserved exactly, because generated code branches on them.
acceptance: W1 and W2 green; the `jit_bs_get_integer` and `jit_bs_get_utf8/16/32` paths are UNTOUCHED in behaviour (they consume the borrow into an integer before any allocation and are correctly safe — proven by their existing tests staying green with no edits)

`BINARY_HELPER_FAILURE` and the `0` (deopt/failure) returns are byte-identical at every site; the JIT ABI signatures in `jit/compiler/ir_helpers.rs:334-354` are UNCHANGED, so generated code is unchanged and no new deopt edge is introduced
The existing `mod gc_release_tests` wall (`runtime_binary_match.rs:382-407`) stays green and unweakened — the refcount-release marking at `:249-253` is not disturbed
Fail-first recorded: revert R3 → W1 and W2 go red at the byte-equality assert → restore

requirements.title: H4 — the map-update helper reserves before it captures
requirements.spec: Per D4: the collecting reserve moves ahead of `map_entries`/`map_pair_terms`, mirroring `put_map` (`closures.rs:462-488`) including its overflow-safe upper-bound arithmetic and its deliberate refusal to trust a `live` operand; the map words are then written with a non-collecting allocation. The `exact` refusal at `runtime_map.rs:68-76` and every `return 0` are preserved.
acceptance: W3 green; `jit_map_new` and `jit_map_update` return the same values as before on every non-collecting path — pinned by the existing map tests staying green with no edits

The word bound is overflow-safe by construction (checked arithmetic, as `map_word_count` at `:142-144` and `put_map` at `closures.rs:468-475` already are) and the `live` value passed to `ensure_space` still roots the full register file
If the drafter takes the D4 alternative (root the vectors rather than hoist the reserve), the handoff states the choice and why; the acceptance above is unchanged either way
Fail-first recorded: revert R4 → W3 goes red at the key/value equality assert → restore

requirements.title: The priority-2 rider — crate-wide stale-Term/pointer capture audit with an auditable site table
requirements.spec: Per D6: enumerate, across `crates/beamr` and `crates/beamr-wasm`, every `Term` local, `Vec<Term>`, `[Term]`, raw `*mut u64`/`*const u64` into heap words, or struct wrapping one, that is USED after a call which can reach `gc::ensure_space` (transitively: `gc::ensure_space`, `gc::collect_minor`, `gc::collect_major`, `jit::runtime::alloc_words`, `jit::runtime::jit_test_heap`, and every non-`_prereserved` `ProcessContext::alloc_*`).
